briefing.text: CALR driver mutations in MPN are exon 9 frameshift indels (type 1 is a 52-bp deletion, type 2 is a 5-bp TTGTC insertion), not point mutations. When you count CALR-mutated samples in data_mutations.txt, keep every CALR row regardless of Variant_Type (DEL/INS included, Frame_Shift_Del/Frame_Shift_Ins), print HGVSp, and match the gene symbol case-insensitively (or by GRCh37 chr19 ~13054500-13055000) so that no CALR rows are missed.
briefing.reason: If you filter to SNPs or missense variants, every CALR driver drops out and the CALR count comes out wrong.

briefing.text: JAK2-mutated status should include JAK2 exon 12 indels and complex variants (e.g. N542-E543del, K539L) as well as V617F. List all JAK2 rows with HGVSp before you define the JAK2-nonmutated group.
briefing.reason: If only V617F counts, exon-12 cases land in the JAK2-nonmutated group by mistake.

briefing.text: Build the denominator from every SAMPLE_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt. A sample with no JAK2 row in the MAF is JAK2-nonmutated, not missing. Cross-tabulate JAK2-mutated against CALR-mutated across all samples, and report the counts and the CALR frequency in each JAK2 group (you can also stratify by MPL).
briefing.reason: Samples absent from the MAF would otherwise be dropped, which shrinks or distorts the JAK2-nonmutated group the hypothesis is about.

briefing.text: The hypothesis makes a universal claim about the JAK2-nonmutated group (no CALR mutation in any of them). What tests it is the number of CALR-mutated samples among the JAK2-nonmutated, not how often CALR and JAK2 co-occur. Published MPN work describes CALR and JAK2 as largely mutually exclusive (Klampfl 2013 and Nangalia 2013, NEJM), so read your cross-tab against that background.
briefing.reason: This keeps the test aimed at the right cell of the table and gives the established biology that the benchmark convention says to weigh.

briefing.text: The clinical table has a single MPN oncotree code, with no ET/PV/PMF subtype and no germline column. Check SOMATIC_STATUS / Mutation_Status for the CALR rows to confirm they are somatic matched-normal calls. The cohort and genes are this study's own, so a missing subtype column is not, on its own, grounds for Not verifiable.
briefing.reason: This heads off a wrong Not verifiable answer and covers the 'somatic' wording in the hypothesis.

shared_assumptions: Both teams defined JAK2 status solely from presence of a JAK2 row in data_mutations.txt (exome calls), assuming a sample with no JAK2 row is JAK2-nonmutated; neither tested this against the study's own per-sample JAK2/MPL annotation, which may come from a separate, more sensitive assay.
Both assumed every CALR row is somatic because SOMATIC_STATUS is 'Matched', without looking at the per-row germline read/allele columns.
Both treated one sample = one patient (true here: 151 samples, PATIENT_ID == SAMPLE_ID) and the whole cohort as in scope (single oncotree code MPN).
unused_evidence: The MAF column 'JAK2/MPL mutation' (values JAK2 / MPL / unmutated) is a study-supplied per-sample driver annotation; neither team used it to define the JAK2-nonmutated group or to cross-check their MAF-derived status.

Columns 'Germline reads', 'Germline allele percentage (%)', 'Tumor allele burden (%)' and 'Tumor reads' would show whether CALR calls are absent from the matched normal (somatic) and at clonal burden; neither team reported them.
TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS in the clinical table was not used (likely irrelevant to this claim).
unresolved_weak_points: Team A: did not list every JAK2 row for exon 12 variants; correctly notes this cannot reduce the CALR-in-JAK2-negative count below its value only if extra JAK2 rows fall on CALR-mutated samples, which their 0 co-occurrence cross-tab already excludes, so effectively resolved.
Team B: one clinical sample has no mutation rows; reported, not material.
Neither team checked that somatic status of CALR calls is supported by the germline allele columns; reported as 'Matched' only.
second_readings: 'Nonmutated JAK2' could mean JAK2 status per the study's own genotyping (the 'JAK2/MPL mutation' annotation) rather than per exome calls; under either reading the test is the CALR count in the JAK2-negative group.

'Myeloproliferative neoplasms with nonmutated JAK2' might be read as JAK2- and MPL-negative (triple-negative context); the universal 'not present in any' claim is falsified by any CALR case in either definition.
challenge.verdict: High trust: the hypothesis is a universal negative and both teams independently found many CALR exon 9 frameshifts among JAK2-negative MPN samples with zero JAK2 co-occurrence, matching established biology; the unused study JAK2/MPL annotation and germline columns are worth a cross-check but are very unlikely to remove every counterexample.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: The MAF has a study-supplied column 'JAK2/MPL mutation' (JAK2 / MPL / unmutated). Cross-tabulate it per sample against your MAF-derived JAK2 status, and count CALR-mutated samples among those the column labels 'unmutated' or 'MPL'. Does any disagreement change who is in your JAK2-nonmutated group or your label?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: For each CALR row, print 'Germline reads', 'Germline allele percentage (%)' and 'Tumor allele burden (%)'. Are any CALR calls present in the matched normal at a germline-like fraction, and would excluding those change your count of somatic CALR in JAK2-nonmutated samples?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: The MAF has a study-supplied column 'JAK2/MPL mutation' (JAK2 / MPL / unmutated) that your method did not use. Cross-tabulate it per sample against your JAK2 definition and count CALR-mutated samples among samples it labels non-JAK2. Does this change your JAK2-unmutated group or your label?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your check list does not show that CALR calls are somatic beyond SOMATIC_STATUS. Print 'Germline allele percentage (%)' and 'Tumor allele burden (%)' for every CALR row; does any CALR call look germline, and does removing it change your conclusion?
